title: God or Son descending as judge (chs. 1–25)
english: Book IV begins: Celsus finds it most shameful that Jews and Christians say a God or God’s Son has come or will come to earth as judge of those here.
translator_notes: Copy-text Koetschau GCS 2–3 Perseus TEI; no Chadwick/ANF Crombie.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B; condensed book CLOSEOUT.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Providence, Israel’s polity, and decay (chs. 26–50)
english: Human nature is unstable; even Israel’s polity decayed. Providence fitted the dignity of the word to changing times without canceling the promise.
translator_notes: Copy-text Koetschau GCS 2–3 Perseus TEI; no Chadwick/ANF Crombie.
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B; condensed book CLOSEOUT.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: Origin of evils — not from God (chs. 51–75)
english: Celsus says evils’ origin is hard for the unphilosophical, yet enough to say evils are not from God but matter-bound; Origen answers from Scripture’s account of good and evil.

title: Elephants’ piety sneer — BOOK IV CLOSEOUT (chs. 76–98)
english: Celsus’s odd claim that elephants swear and know God better than we do is answered and dismissed; Book IV closes.
